headline: High: Rasa can exfiltrate conversation data over allowlisted APIs while the zoomcamp profile provides no isolation or runtime controls, creating a default data-leakage and cascading-error risk.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: No direct shared channel is documented between data-engineering-zoomcamp and rasa, so prompt injection is not provably present. However, rasa exposes chat APIs and can ingest user text, while the zoomcamp profile is a course/repo with no runtime isolation details; if content is manually bridged, injection is possible but not default.
conditions: IF an operator copies zoomcamp-generated text into a Rasa conversation or prompt
IF Rasa is configured to treat external text as instructions without sanitization
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate workspaces
Disable copy-paste bridging between outputs and prompts
Add a fixed instruction prefix that ignores quoted content
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging before any handoff

B_data_leakage.rationale: Rasa touches text and voice and sends traffic through allowlisted messaging APIs, so conversation data can leave the local boundary. The zoomcamp profile has no data classes touched and no egress, but the pair still creates a default leakage path for any user text routed through Rasa; the exact data class is limited, so medium fits.
conditions: IF sensitive text or voice content is routed into Rasa
IF any connected channel forwards transcripts to a third-party messaging API
mitigations: Restrict Rasa channels to a test tenant
Redact secrets before messages reach Rasa
Turn off logging of full conversation payloads
Separate any course materials from chat transcripts
requires-engineering: enforce data-class filtering at ingress

C_capability_conflict.rationale: The zoomcamp profile is non-runnable and shows no write surfaces, while rasa supports multiple external chat APIs but no filesystem or git write capability is documented. Because neither profile shows overlapping mutable resources, a write-write conflict is not evidenced; uncertainty stays low rather than none because the docs are incomplete.
conditions: IF both agents are attached to the same mutable workspace outside the documented profiles
IF an orchestrator grants both write access to a shared resource
mitigations: Keep each agent on separate storage
Avoid shared git or database targets
Run only one writer per resource
requires-engineering: add locking around shared state

D_cascading_error.rationale: Rasa is a downstream action-taking chatbot framework, and its dialogue understanding can consume upstream text. The zoomcamp profile can generate instructional content, but no verification step is documented before Rasa would act on it, so A-to-B propagation is plausible in default integrations and can misroute responses or actions.
conditions: IF zoomcamp output is used as training or response content for Rasa
IF Rasa routes an unverified upstream answer to a user-facing channel
mitigations: Require human review before publishing responses
Add a validation step for any imported content
Limit Rasa to canned intents only
Log source provenance for every generated reply
requires-engineering: add automated fact-checking before action

E_compliance.rationale: No PHI, residency, or retention mismatch is documented for either profile, and both are open-source docs-only entries. The only concrete compliance concern is that Rasa handles text and voice over external channels, so if regulated data were introduced, policy gaps could appear; the zoomcamp profile itself does not add a separate compliance burden.
conditions: IF regulated text or voice data is sent through Rasa channels
IF the operator applies a retention policy to one agent but not the other
mitigations: Avoid regulated data in chat flows
Publish a short retention policy for transcripts
Disable transcript export where possible
Separate training materials from operational logs
